Will AI take your job? Here are the big numbers, by 2030, worldwide.

THE NUMBERS (World Economic Forum, Future of Jobs Report 2025, a survey of more than 1,000 employers):
• 170 million new jobs created
• 92 million jobs displaced
• Net: about +78 million jobs
• 39% of the key skills in a job are expected to change
• Fastest-growing skill: AI and big data

WHAT IT MEANS: the bigger risk isn't a robot taking your job. It's the job changing around you while your skills stay the same.

THE CATCH: these are employer forecasts, not guarantees, and they vary a lot by industry and country.

Do this: pick one AI skill your job needs and practise it 15 minutes a day this week.

Send this to the friend who's job hunting.

What your government pension pays, 2026 🇨🇦

Average new CPP at 65: about $858 a month
Most you can get at 65: about $1,508 a month
Start CPP at 60: up to 36% less, for life
Wait until 70: up to 42% more, for life
OAS at 65 to 74: up to about $763 a month

Why it matters: together, that's well short of most people's bills. Your TFSA and RRSP fill the gap.

Do this: log in to My Service Canada Account and check your CPP estimate. It takes 5 minutes.

Send this to the friend counting on CPP.

#CPP #OAS #retirementcanada #personalfinancecanada #moneyfoundations

Focus science, in 5 numbers

A new habit takes about 66 days to feel automatic.
Switching tasks can eat up to 40% of your productive time.
A walk lifted creative ideas by about 60%.
People who wrote down when and where they'd exercise: 91% did it.
Strong coffee 6 hours before bed cut sleep by more than an hour.

Do this: this week, try one row. Start with a 10-minute walk before your hardest task.

Save this for a slow Monday.

#focus #habits #productivity #deepwork #studytips

Late on the RESP? Here's the grant you can still get 🇨🇦

Start at birth: up to $7,200
Start at age 5: up to $7,200
Start at age 10: up to $7,200
Start at age 12: up to $6,000

posts.caption:
Nodding along in AI meetings? 6 AI words, decoded 📖

Model: the trained AI itself (GPT, Gemini, Claude and Llama are model families).
Prompt: what you type or say to it.
Token: a word-piece. AI reads and writes in tokens; a short English word is often one token, a long one can be several.
Training: how it learned, by studying huge amounts of text and learning which words tend to come next.
Hallucination: a confident mistake, an answer that sounds right and isn't.
Agent: AI that takes actions, like clicking through a website for you, not just answering.

Why it matters: when you can explain these in one sentence, AI stops being magic and starts being a tool you can judge.

Do this: this week, use one of these words at work and explain it in one sentence.

Send this to the friend nodding along in meetings.

Follow to learn what AI can really do, one real test a day.

#ai #learnai #chatgpt #aiglossary #futureofwork #hourback

New baby in Ontario? One box on the birth registration starts your Canada Child Benefit.

HOW IT WORKS: when you register the birth online with ServiceOntario's Newborn Registration Service, choose "Canada child benefits". With your OK, your details go straight to the CRA. No separate form.

HOW MUCH: up to $8,157 a year for each child under 6, paid monthly (July 2026 to June 2027). It's income-tested, so it gets smaller as family income goes up.

THE 3 MISTAKES TO AVOID:
1. Applying again through My Account or form RC66 after you ticked the box. The CRA already has it.
2. Forgetting the SIN. The main caregiver (the parent who applies) needs theirs ready.
3. Skipping tax returns. Both parents need to file every year, even with little or no income, or the payments can stop.

THE SAME 15 MINUTES ALSO: the Newborn Registration Service bundle can order the birth certificate and apply for baby's SIN, which you'll need for an RESP later.

Do this: before the birth, put both parents' SINs in one note on your phone, so registration takes one sitting.

The rule that stays: one box, every month.

Send this to someone expecting a baby.

#newparents #canadachildbenefit #ontarioparents #babymoney #expectingparents

The primary caregiver applies and gives their SIN. Maximum CCB, July 2026 to June 2027: up to $8,157 a year per child under 6 (canada.ca; income-tested).
